newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schwarz Pharma to market new drug in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Schwarz Pharma to market new drug in U.S..

text.p: German drug company Schwarz Pharma AG said Thursday it had reached an agreement with Canadian company Axcan Pharma Inc. to sell Schwarz Pharma's new liver drug in the United States.
Schwarz Pharma, fresh from entering a similar marketing agreement with U.S. company Lynx Therapeutics, also said it was taking a 4 percent stake in Axcan Pharma.
The two companies will each hold a 50 percent stake in Axcan Schwarz, the newly established company, and estimate sales of the URSO liver drug could total $100 million annually.

Schwarz Pharma beat out competitors for rights to jointly market URSO, used to treat the liver disease primary biliary cirrhosis, only days after U.S. health officials approved the drug and Axcan said it was looking for a marketing partner.
At the time, the Canadian company said it was in talks with several U.S. pharmaceutical companies eager to market the new drug.
Since floating its shares on the stock market last year, Schwarz Pharma has entered a number of joint ventures in the United States in a bid to strengthen its international sales base.

The company, receiving top marks from analysts as a promising small drug company, has focused its resources on forming marketing agreements for innovative drugs rather than concentrating resources largely on building up its own drug pipeline.
Schwarz Pharma said Axcan will seek to receive U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration approval for the drug, to be used to treat other diseases, including a form of hepatitis, as well.
